meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Akt phosphorylates TSC2, disabling the complex. Growth-factor signalling works by removing a brake, not by pressing an accelerator.
data.mechanism_beginner: Akt tags TSC2 to disable it. Growth signals work by releasing a brake, not by pressing a gas pedal.
data.boundary: In mouse liver, Akt phosphorylation of TSC2 is the main route by which insulin switches on mTORC1, but feeding activates hepatic mTORC1 without it; that response needs dietary protein instead (KAL2026). The biochemical mechanism itself was shown in cultured human cells (INO2002).
